structured.approach: Attempt 4 fixes the G3 refusal. The exact coverage figures from the CI run do not appear in any input or tool view this step can cite: the spine records the CI result only as "Sources compile". So the CI result is now stated without those figures, in claims and in task.code.md alike: compile passes, the existing tests pass, static checks are clean, and coverage is below the 90% gate from org.engineering_stack, with the missed lines described by what they are. The exact report stays in the spine's own CI record. I ran /usr/bin/python3 ci.py again (same outcome) and rewrote task.code.md in full. Every number left in a claim appears in the item that claim cites. The code is unchanged since attempt 1 and follows feat.design B3.2 and task.components BC-1 to BC-6. Unit tests (BC-7) are outside this step's write scope (src/ap_aging/, docs/, README.md), so I did not add them and did not try to raise coverage another way. The coverage shortfall goes to BE-06 as a non-blocking open question.

claims.text: overdue_with_risk(invoices: Iterable[Dict], as_of: date, risk_by_vendor: Dict[str, str]) -> List[Dict] is in src/ap_aging/aging.py with the design's signature and docstring, and it reuses days_past_due.

The function skips paid invoices with the same inv.get("paid") test as aging_buckets. It lists an invoice only when days > OVERDUE_AFTER_DAYS, with OVERDUE_AFTER_DAYS = 30, so exactly 30 days is not listed, and it never calls bucket_for.

Rows have exactly the keys id, vendor, days, amount and risk. risk falls back to 'unknown', a missing vendor raises KeyError, the amount is Decimal quantised with TWO_PLACES = Decimal("0.01"), and rows are sorted by days descending, then id ascending.
overdue_rows_to_json(rows: Iterable[Dict]) -> str returns the CT-1 JSON array with keys in CT-1 order, days as int and amount as a two-decimal string, without passing through float.
src/ap_aging/__init__.py exports overdue_with_risk and overdue_rows_to_json in __all__ and sets __version__ to 1.5.0, a minor step from 1.4.0.
BUCKETS, days_past_due, bucket_for, aging_buckets and tests/test_aging.py are unchanged.

CI compiles, the existing unit tests pass and the static checks report no issues. Line coverage is below the 90% gate, so CI fails on coverage only. The uncovered code is the bodies of the two new functions plus one existing bucket_for branch.

README.md and docs/ were updated as the brief requires. A new docs/aging.md gives a module overview and the new functions with signatures, inputs, outputs and examples, and README.md lists the public functions and links to it.
Changes stay within the allowed write scope (src/ap_aging/, docs/, README.md). Nothing was committed or pushed.
The suggested commit message starts with the story IDs, as the engineering stack requires.

open_questions: CQ-BE-2 (non-blocking): CI fails the coverage gate (below 90%) because the new functions have no tests yet, and tests/ is outside BE-05's write scope. BE-06 needs to add tests/test_overdue.py as planned in task.components BC-7 and confirm the CI pass there.

Carried (non-blocking), with the interim designs implemented: TQ-3 (CT-1 approval), TQ-9 (KeyError for a missing vendor), TQ-1 (bucket_for(30)), DQ-1 (production wiring of CT-1), DQ-2 (rounding mode), PQ-2 (meaning of days and the id tie-break).

In CI, compile, the existing tests and static checks pass, but CI fails overall because coverage is below the 90% gate. The new code has no tests yet because tests/ is outside this step's write scope; BE-06 is expected to add tests/test_overdue.py to clear the gate.
